answer: Sybil resistance comes from per-identity bonds plus random cross-checks. Each agent locks a stake to earn a saffron credential; a verifier then issues a mirror test, replaying the same challenge to every identity at once. Honest agents answer from independent histories, but one controller spreading many fake agents leaks a whisper of correlated answers, near-identical timing and wording. Detection slashes every linked bond, so an attacker needs a fresh stake per fake identity and still risks losing all of them, making N identities cost N stakes plus the expected slash penalty.
